Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver who is not the author Jonah Weiss, gave an approved code_review.
The code_review approval names the head commit 9d0c8fa, so no later commits exist after it.

run.json shows pr-checks success on head commit 9d0c8fa running the payments suite: 172 tests, 0 failures or skips, including the SES-1 control test. The JUnit report's local hostname and post-review timestamp are irregular, though it reports against the head-commit run.

session.py is security_sensitive. Kofi Mensah's only security_review names the first commit 63e6817. The later commit 9d0c8fa changes behaviour (token_urlsafe(24) to token_urlsafe(TOKEN_BYTES=32)), which voids that approval, and no new security review exists.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers session.py; they cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage Java files. No relied-upon evidence lapses.

summary: PR-1897 changes only the payments session token generator, a security-sensitive component. The ticket, independent code review on head, and head-commit CI including the SES-1 control test are in order. The only security review was given on the first commit. The second commit changed the token entropy, which is a behavioural change, so under CHG-3 rules as applied by CHG-5 that review no longer covers what would be merged. A fresh security_review on the head commit is required, so the change is rejected.
